deities: Lord Shiva (as Baidyanath, the Divine Physician)

history.dynasty: CONFLICT (verify): traditional accounts credit Puran Mal (ancestor of the Nagavanshi dynasty) with the original 8th-century construction; the current structure is attributed to Raja Man Singh (16th c.); other sources date the current structure to the 18th c.
history.period: Legendary origins (Ravana-era); stone structure dated variously 8th c.-18th c.
history.summary: Baidyanath Dham is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva and also one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (Sati's heart is said to have fallen here), a rare convergence of both sanctities. Legend holds that Ravana performed penance and carried the Jyotirlinga toward Lanka, but Vishnu (in disguise) caused it to be set down at Deoghar, where it became immovable. The 72-foot Nagara-style shikhara houses the svayambhu lingam within a complex of 22 temples. Maithili priests (pandas) took over temple charge in the 16th century; Raja Man Singh is credited with the current structure. During Shravan, the Shravani Mela brings millions of kanwariyas carrying Ganga water 105 km on foot from Sultanganj.

name: Baidyanath Dham (Baba Baidyanath Temple)
town_description: Deoghar, the 'Abode of Gods', is the cultural capital of Jharkhand and headquarters of Deoghar district in the Santhal Parganas division. It is primarily known for the Baidyanath Jyotirlinga, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, which makes it one of eastern India's busiest pilgrimage centres, especially during the Shravan month Kanwar Yatra. The city became a municipality in 1869 and is surrounded by small hills including Nandan Pahar, Trikut Pahar and Tapovan Pahar, with the Ajay river flowing nearby.

travel.railway: Deoghar Railway Station, approx. 2-3 km; Jasidih Junction (on the Howrah-Patna-Delhi line), approx. 7-8 km (verify)
travel.road: Well connected by road to Jasidih, Dumka, Ranchi (~250-280 km), Patna (~255 km) and Kolkata; the temple is inside Deoghar town (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather, manageable crowds); Shravan (July-August) is the peak Kanwar Yatra season with very heavy crowds
